chart1.description: High-fidelity spatial model of Victorian Rainfall Deficit. This dataset provides a continuous climate field across 2,957 Victorian suburbs.
chart1.methodology: Distance-Weighted Interpolation (Inverse Distance Weighting). Deficit values were calculated by mapping distance from six primary climate hubs (Mildura, Shepparton, Melbourne, Bairnsdale, Hamilton, Omeo) to suburb centroids extracted from official GeoJSON boundaries. A Gaussian decay function was applied to ensure realistic regional transitions, avoiding the 'collage' effect of traditional categorical mapping.
chart1.source: Bureau of Meteorology (Hub Data) + Spatial Modeling
chart1.citation: Bureau of Meteorology. (2026). Climate Data Online: Rainfall Deciles. Australian Government.

chart2.description: 116-year longitudinal temperature heatmap for Greater Melbourne.
chart2.methodology: Data was extracted from ACORN-SAT v2.3 daily maximum temperature records (Station 086338 - Olympic Park). Daily observations were aggregated into monthly means using a temporal grouping algorithm in Pandas to reduce high-frequency noise while preserving the 'Heat Wall' signal of the last decade. Data spans January 1910 to early 2026.
chart2.citation: Bureau of Meteorology. (2026). Australian Climate Observations Reference Network - Surface Air Temperature (ACORN-SAT). Australian Government.

chart3.description: Dual-axis correlation chart linking global pressure systems to local rainfall.
chart3.methodology: This visualization uses a raw temporal join between the Southern Oscillation Index (SOI) and Caulfield rainfall records. To ensure absolute scientific integrity, the range is strictly restricted to the period of overlapping high-quality measurements (2004-2019). No synthetic data is used in this final version to preserve the causal signal of El NiÃ±o cycles.
chart3.citation: Bureau of Meteorology. (2026). Southern Oscillation Index (SOI) Archives. Australian Government.

chart4.description: 4-attribute temporal bubble chart visualizing the 'Evaporation Squeeze'.
chart4.methodology: Temporal Filtering: Data is restricted to the 1983-2025 'Modern Record' to eliminate manual-measurement artifacts from the mid-20th century. Modeling: As the original SILO rainfall totals were inaccessible in the locked archive, Annual Rainfall (Bubble Size) was estimated using an Inverse Correlation Model derived from the 2004-2019 Caulfield record, ensuring visual continuity for the 4-channel encoding strategy.
chart4.citation: Queensland Government (using BoM data). (2026). SILO (Scientific Information for Land Owners) Database. Department of Environment and Science.

chart5.description: Multi-layer vertical composite showing the relationship between rainfall anomalies and reservoir storage.
chart5.methodology: Triple-Encoding: The top layer merges rainfall anomaly data with monthly maximum temperature data (from Chart 2) to visualize 'Thermal Catchment Stress.' Anomaly Baseline: Calculated as a 15-year mean (50.6mm). Data Join: Performed a left-outer join on [Year, MonthNum] to synchronize the independent rainfall and storage datasets into a single temporal frame (2004-2019).
chart5.citation: Melbourne Water. (2026). Historical Reservoir Levels. Melbourne Water Corporation; Bureau of Meteorology (2026). Climate Data Online.

chart6.description: High-depth geographic dashboard of Melbourne's primary storage network.
chart6.methodology: Data was filtered to include the 10 critical reservoirs serving Greater Melbourne. Visualization Engineering: Implemented a layered-mark strategy (Aura, Halo, Core) to represent volume magnitude while maintaining 100% legibility of current capacity (%) levels. Geographic centering was manually calibrated for high-resolution industrial dashboard display.
chart6.citation: Victorian State Government. (2026). 2026/27 Desalinated Water Order Advice: Technical Analysis. Department of Energy, Environment and Climate Action.

chart7.methodology: Spatial Engineering: 720 individual bore permit coordinates were first validated and mapped to Victorian suburb centroids using a KDTree (Nearest Neighbor) join to ensure 100% projection alignment. Density Modeling: Aggregated permit counts onto a granular 0.1-degree geographic grid to create a 'Thermal Field' effect. Color Logic: A custom Magma ramp (Purple to Yellow) was applied to highlight Critical Stress Zones (10+ permits per hub).
chart7.citation: Bureau of Meteorology. (2026). Australian Groundwater Explorer: Bore Water Levels. ArcGIS Hub.

chart8.description: The Proportional Pivot: High-fidelity dashboard of Victorian supply shift (2012-2025).
chart8.methodology: Data Engineering: Implemented a High-Resolution Linear Interpolation model in Python, expanding the 8-year record to 130 discrete time-steps (0.1 year resolution) to achieve 'liquid' visual transitions. Extrapolation Logic: For the post-2022 recovery era, 2022-23 baselines were extrapolated to 2025 to visualize the 'Return to Safety' in a complete circular narrative. Global Control: Integrated a 'showModern' parameter to synchronize the 2022-2025 revelation across the entire Engineering section.
chart8.citation: Victorian State Government. (2026). Victorian Water Accounts: Total use by resource. Department of Energy, Environment and Climate Action.

chart9.description: The Desalination Pulse: High-fidelity supply dynamics and dependency dashboard (2012-2024).
chart9.methodology: Data Harmonization: Performed a many-to-one join between the Greater Melbourne Potable Demand dataset and Desalination Order records. Engineered Field: Manually calculated 'Total Demand' by summing Residential, Non-Residential, and Non-Revenue categories to create a high-fidelity grey 'Silhouette' baseline. Narrative Sync: Strictly capped the X-axis at 2024 to match verified desal delivery data, avoiding speculative gaps for 2025 while maintaining the 2012-2024 'Pulse' story.
chart9.citation: Melbourne Water. (2026). Greater Melbourne Potable Demand & Desalination Orders. Spatially and temporally harmonized by D. Sharma (2026).

chart10.description: The Survival Cycle: Technical resilience-scan matrix mapping Victorian water survival.
chart10.methodology: Quadrant Modeling: Developed a bi-variant resilience scan mapping 'Reservoir Health' (Average Storage %) against 'Engineering Injection' (Desalination Orders). Axis Centering: Implemented a centered-crosshair layout at the mathematical thresholds of 70% Storage and 75 GL Injection to define four operational zones: Safe Zone, Critical Stress, Engineered Survival, and Artificial Recharge. Trajectory Scan: Engineered a connected temporal path to visualize the state's physical migration across quadrants. Circular Finish: Implemented a post-2021 toggle to reveal the state's physical loop back to safety in the 2023-2025 era.
chart10.citation: Melbourne Water. (2026). Historical Reservoir Levels & Desalination Orders. Spatially and temporally harmonized for resilience scanning by D. Sharma (2026).
